voronoi_tesselation module¶

Voronoi tesselation of space using scipy

Use the Qhull library (can compute Delaunay triangulation and Voronoi diagram). Cannot compute Voronoi volumes or weighted Voronoi diagrams.

voronoi_tesselation.find_vertex_index_in_region()¶

Locates the relative index of the vertex absolute index “vertex_value” within the region “regions[index_region]” Useful when knowing that an absolute vertex index value is present and when looking for the adjacent vertices

Parameters:
  • regions (list of lists) – Indices of vertices in each revised Voronoi regions.
  • index_region (int, index of the region to check) –
  • vertex_value (value of the vertex one wants to look for) –
Returns:

  • found (boolean, indicates if the vertex_value actually exists in the region)
  • index_vertex (int, relative index WITHIN the region)

Example : Region is [4, 7, 9, 8, 5] and we’re looking for the vertex 9 return index_vertex = 2

voronoi_tesselation.generate_hexagonal_seed()¶

Create seed points (Voronoi center) on a controlled or “noisy” (with a bit of noise) hexagonal lattice, and applies periodic boundary conditions.

Parameters:
  • point_number (int) – Number of seed point to create
  • boxsize (float) – Length of the axis for observation box (assumed square for now)
  • lattice_noise (float) – Intensity of the noise applied to the lattice seed points
Returns:

  • generated_points (ndarray of ndarray) – Array of seed points on a lattice (of coordinates x,y)
  • generated_angles (ndarray) – Array of randomly drawn angles in radians
  • generated_polarities (ndarray of double) – Array of polarity vectors (cos theta_i, sin theta_i), initialized with random initial values
  • (in the future maybe) (flag)
voronoi_tesselation.generate_periodic_voronoi_cells()¶

Copy the initialized points around the observation box of size “boxsize”

Parameters:
  • points (numpy array of arrays) – (x,y) coordinates of the Voronoi centers
  • boxsize (float) – Size of a side of the observation box (assumed square-shaped)
Returns:

extended_points – (x,y) coordinates of the Voronoi centers and their copy
Return type:

numpy array of arrays
voronoi_tesselation.generate_periodic_voronoi_cells_2()¶

Copy the initialized points around the observation box of size “boxsize”, over the 8 nearest regions C-like version (250+ times faster than the pure python)

Parameters:
  • points (numpy array of arrays) – (x,y) coordinates of the Voronoi centers
  • boxsize (float) – Size of a side of the observation box (assumed square-shaped)
Returns:

extended_points – (x,y) coordinates of the Voronoi centers and their copy
Return type:

numpy array of arrays
voronoi_tesselation.get_nearest_neighbors()¶

Computes the Euclidean distance between the point vertices[region[index]] and the other vertices WITHIN a region.

Parameters:
  • region (a single finite region from the Voronoi tesselation) –
  • index (the index of the point of interest of which we are looking for the nearest neighbors) –
  • vertices (a list of lists (vertices)) –
Returns:

nearest_neighbors
Return type:

numpy array with indices referring to the vertices list ordered from closest to furthest
voronoi_tesselation.get_polygons_properties_2d()¶

Computes the perimeters and the areas of every cell defined by the regions and vertices passed as parameters

Parameters:
  • regions (list of lists) – Indices of vertices in each revised Voronoi regions.
  • vertices (numpy array) – Coordinates for revised Voronoi vertices. Same as coordinates of input vertices, with ‘points at infinity’ appended to the end.
Returns:

  • None (None) – Placeholder for backward compatibility
  • perimeters (numpy array) – Perimeter of each region in regions treated
  • areas (numpy array) – Area of each region in regions treated
voronoi_tesselation.get_polygons_properties_2d_Qhull()¶

Extract the perimeter and area for each finite polygon in 2D Partially Cython typed.

Parameters:
  • regions (list of lists) – Indices of vertices in each revised Voronoi regions.
  • vertices (numpy array) – Coordinates for revised Voronoi vertices. Same as coordinates of input vertices, with ‘points at infinity’ appended to the end.
Returns:

  • properties_index (numpy array) – List of index for each region in regions treated (probably not useful since perimeter and area are already acquired in the order of region in regions)
  • properties_perimeter (numpy array) – Perimeter of each region in regions treated
  • properties_area (numpy array) – Area of each region in regions treated Warning : In 2D : ConvexHull.area is the perimeter, while ConvexHull.volume is the area
voronoi_tesselation.get_shared_vertices()¶

Determines which vertices are shared between regions[index_interest] and the other regions.

Parameters:
  • regions (list of lists) – Indices of vertices in each revised Voronoi regions.
  • index_interest (int) – Index of the region of interest
Returns:

  • list_adjacent_regions (list of indices) – Returns a list with the absolute indices of a “region” in the regions list obtained from voronoi_finite_polygons_2d
  • list_shared_vertices (list of lists) – Returns a list of list of format [(list of shared vertices] between region[index_interest] and region[index_neighbor])
voronoi_tesselation.is_sorted_counterclockwise()¶

Compute the determinant of the orientation matrix for three vertices per region of a simple convex polygon. If positive, the polygon is sorted counterclockwise. Otherwise it is sorted clockwise (assuming there is self intersection or hole in the polygon)

Parameters:
  • regions (list of lists) – Indices of vertices in each revised Voronoi regions.
  • vertices (numpy array) – Coordinates for revised Voronoi vertices. Same as coordinates of input vertices, with ‘points at infinity’ appended to the end.
Returns:

sorted_counterclockwise_truth_table – Contains True if the determinant is positive (and the polygon is sorted counter clockwise), False otherwise
Return type:

np array
voronoi_tesselation.plot_contour()¶

Plot the contour of the observation box for cell symmetry observation

Parameters:boxsize (float (or int)) – Size of the observation box.
Returns:
Return type:Nothing.
voronoi_tesselation.plot_polygons()¶

Graphical function to plot polygons by circling through their vertices.

Note that while the Voronoi regions are finite, they may still go beyond the box

Parameters:
  • vor (A Voronoi object) –
  • regions (list of lists) – Indices of vertices in each revised Voronoi regions.
  • vertices (list of lists) – Coordinates for revised Voronoi vertices. Same as coordinates of input vertices, with ‘points at infinity’ appended to the end.
voronoi_tesselation.sort_vertices_counterclockwise()¶

Reverse the regions where sorted_counterclockwise_truth_table is false.

Parameters:
  • regions (list of lists) – Indices of vertices in each revised Voronoi regions.
  • vertices (numpy array) – Coordinates for revised Voronoi vertices. Same as coordinates of input vertices, with ‘points at infinity’ appended to the end.
  • sorted_counterclockwise_truth_table (np array) – Contains True if the determinant is positive (and the polygon is sorted counter clockwise), False otherwise
Returns:

regions_sorted_counterclockwise – Indices of vertices in each revised Voronoi regions sorted counter clockwisely
Return type:

list of lists
voronoi_tesselation.voronoi_finite_polygons_2d()¶

Reconstruct infinite voronoi regions in a 2D diagram to finite regions.

Parameters:
  • vor (Voronoi) – Input diagram
  • radius (float, optional) – Distance to ‘points at infinity’.
  • point_number (int) – Limits the number of regions to sort. If None is given, the sorting algorithm will run through all the regions, including the ones outside the observation box
Returns:

  • regions (list of lists) – Indices of vertices in each revised Voronoi regions. Vertices are sorted counter-clockwise.
  • vertices (list of lists) – Coordinates for revised Voronoi vertices. Same as coordinates of input vertices, with ‘points at infinity’ appended to the end.
